selected_gaps.gap: (additive; leaf sites L_deltamodel, L_restgp, L_concrete_residual) No residual-correction leaf provides a correction whose expected effect is non-negative where local reference evidence is thin. The Δ-model leaf finds corrections are needed most exactly where training coverage is sparsest, but it relies on acquiring new labels there. The residual-GP and physics-residual leaves say nothing about what their correction does to a query with no close training analogue. A fixed offline benchmark offers no label acquisition, so the question is open in exactly the regime where it matters. — stakes: on steels (n = 312) a handful of atypical alloys dominate MAE, so a correction that extrapolates wrongly there erases or reverses the average gain. In discovery use, the novel compositions are the ones whose predictions are acted on, so a correction that is harmful off-support costs real experiments.

companion_dependency.object: deployment-matched correction instances: for each inner-held-out training composition i, the tuple (pair-excluded analogue estimate A_i, competing base prediction f^(-m(i))(x_i), support descriptor s_i, label y_i)
companion_dependency.producer: the assumption pivot: re-specifying the correction's observation model so that the query's base prediction, every borrowed neighbour residual and the transfer model all come from refits that saw neither the query nor that neighbour (pair-excluded refits inside the training fold)
companion_dependency.consumer: fitting of the damping map lambda(s) and selection of the kernel bandwidth h, neighbourhood size k_nn and distance rho, by minimising the realised loss of (1 - lambda) f + lambda A on those instances
companion_dependency.removal_effect: without the manufactured instances lambda must be set by a variance or distance formula (partial pooling or an applicability-domain cut-off), which is the flagged C_shrinkage / C_applicability_domain node and is blind to the near-duplicate double-counting failure the pivot exposes

selected_gaps.companion_rationale: Step 2a chain A -> O -> B: the assumption pivot (A) replaces the tacit premise 'a neighbour's out-of-fold residual is exchangeable with the deployed stack's residual at the query' by a fold-matched transfer, and its construction yields O, a set of training-fold instances whose base prediction and borrowed residuals stand in exactly the fold relation that an outer test composition will; the signal-manufacturing move (B) consumes O as a label-free-at-deployment supervisory target for the damping map, which is the only way to learn where the correction helps when, offline, no new labels can be acquired where support is thin.
selected_gaps.selection_rationale: This is the construction gap whose closure the user's pipeline depends on: a local out-of-fold residual correction is only worth adding to a cross-fitted stack if its expected effect is non-negative where evidence is thin, and at n = 312 with no label acquisition that property must be built, not hoped for. The audit-and-pivot move closes it by naming the load-bearing premise the naive correction rests on (borrowed out-of-fold residuals are exchangeable with the refit stack's residual at the query, which fails where the refit has absorbed a near-duplicate neighbour) and building the correction under the relaxed premise; OCCUPIED-SOURCE CONSTRAINT for Phase 2.2: the residual-on-input transfer (n_residual_on_input, C_local_smoothing), distance damping (C_applicability_domain), variance shrinkage (C_shrinkage) and per-query expert weighting (C_moe, C_des) are occupied nodes and may appear only as substrate, so the novelty must come from the fold-relation mismatch between deployed refit and borrowed residual, which no lineage node occupies; heterogeneous_decomposition (partition queries by support regime) and adapt_via_conditioning (neighbour context at inference) were rejected because their natural artifacts land on C_applicability_domain and L_iclfm respectively.

phase2_select/phase2_select_output.json.deliverable_coverage: method — anchor gap -> assumption_audit_and_pivot defines the runnable fold-matched local residual correction; the Step 2a companion self_supervised_signal_engineering manufactures the deployment-matched instances on which its damping is fit, which together make the correction's in-fold expected effect non-negative by construction of the admissible family (lambda = 0 admissible).

user_direction_disposition.user_wanted: Transfer cross-fitted stacking of diverse experts followed by a novelty-damped local out-of-fold residual correction (confirmed in my earlier SIG-Net paper) to composition-based materials property prediction on the four Matbench v0.1 composition tasks (steels, expt_gap, expt_is_metal, glass)
quoted_spans_from_user_query: followed by a novelty-damped local out-of-fold residual correction (confirmed in my earlier SIG-Net paper)
the four Matbench v0.1 composition tasks (steels, expt_gap, expt_is_metal, glass)
Constraints: CPU-only, official Matbench folds, honest nested cross-validation for every choice, no test-fold use.
user_direction_disposition.chosen: The candidate keeps the user's pipeline shape and constraints: a cross-fitted stack of diverse CPU-trainable experts, then a damped local out-of-fold residual correction, every choice made by nested CV inside the official training folds. It modifies two internals of the correction. (1) The borrowed residual is fold-matched: it is added to the prediction of the refit that excluded the neighbour, not to the full refit. (2) The damping is not a fixed novelty (distance) schedule; it is a map over support descriptors fit on deployment-matched instances manufactured inside the training fold.
user_direction_disposition.why_adopted: The anchor gap (non-negative correction where local evidence is thin, offline) is exactly the property the user's correction stage needs on these tasks, so selecting it on the usual criteria lands on the user's direction rather than away from it. The direction is not transferred unchanged, because the regression map in method_lineage notes that stacking, local residual transfer and novelty damping each already occupy a node. The publishable increment is therefore the fold-relation fix and the manufactured damping signal. It is not the transfer of SIG-Net's components to a new domain, and SIG-Net is treated as the user's origin of the pipeline, not as indexed prior art.

phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.title: Fold-Matched Local Residual Correction for Cross-Fitted Composition Stacks on Small Matbench Tasks

intervention_object.acts_on: the out-of-fold residuals of a cross-fitted stack of composition experts, as they are transferred from training compositions to a query and added to the stack's prediction
intervention_object.operator: a fold-matched analogue estimate (neighbour label plus the neighbour-excluded refit's predicted difference between query and neighbour), blended with the full-refit stack prediction by a damping map over support descriptors that is fit on deployment-matched instances manufactured from pair-excluded refits inside the training fold
intervention_object.decision_variables: the damping value lambda(s_q) per query (from a low-capacity admissible family that contains lambda = 0), plus the nested-CV-selected kernel bandwidth h, neighbourhood size k_nn, composition distance rho, residual scale tau and expert set E

phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.hook: We construct a fold-matched local residual correction for cross-fitted composition stacks whose damping is fit on deployment-matched instances, because the naive out-of-fold correction should hurt most at the near-duplicate end of composition space, not at the off-support end that novelty damping guards. The reason is that a neighbour's out-of-fold residual double-counts an error that the refit stack has already absorbed by training on that neighbour.
phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.hook_shape_rationale: (i) Shape (a). The named metric is outer-test MAE (and log loss / probability AUROC on the classification tasks), stratified by the distance delta_1 from each test composition to its nearest training composition. The prediction that the naive correction's excess error over the uncorrected stack concentrates in the smallest-delta_1 stratum, and grows with an expert's capacity to interpolate its training points, is the opposite of the off-support failure that the Δ-model leaf (semanticscholar:398586587c1f70079b3b60825e93ff651a519ff9) and every distance-based damping scheme anticipate. (ii) Shape (b) was viable, by citing the stacking substrate's tacit assumption that level-1 inputs from out-of-fold models are interchangeable with full-refit outputs, but that mismatch is a known (if usually ignored) property of stacking, so reframing it louder would not pass the unnamed-in-practice test; the non-obvious content is where along the support axis it bites for a local correction, which is an empirical direction claim.

phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.core_mechanism: Notation. Fix an official Matbench v0.1 outer fold k with training set T_k; all objects below are computed from T_k only. Partition T_k at random into J inner folds P_1..P_J (J an integer, at least 3, chosen once on the cost-variance trade-off and reported); m(j) denotes the inner fold of training composition j. A cross-fitted stack F combines experts e in E (admissible members: gradient-boosted trees or random forest on Magpie features, MODNet on MatMiner features, TabPFN v2 on Magpie features run on CPU, kNN on element-fraction vectors; E chosen by nested CV) with non-negative level-1 weights beta fit on inner out-of-fold predictions (Breiman NNLS for regression, a non-negative logistic level-1 for classification). This stack is substrate, not contribution. Write F^full for the stack whose experts are refit on all of T_k, F^(-m) for the one whose experts saw T_k minus P_m, and F^(-m,-m') for the pair-excluded refit that saw T_k minus (P_m union P_m'). Residuals live on a scale tau chosen by nested CV (raw target for regression; probability or logit working residual for classification), and r_j = y_j - F^(-m(j))(x_j) is j's out-of-fold residual. Audited premise. The naive local out-of-fold correction predicts F^full(x_q) + sum_j w_qj r_j, with kernel weights w_qj = K(rho(q,j)/h) normalised over the k_nn nearest training compositions under a composition distance rho (admissible: Element Mover's Distance via the ElMD package, or Euclidean on standardised Magpie vectors). This silently assumes that r_j estimates the deployed stack's error at q. Algebraically, the naive estimate equals A_q + M_q, where A_q = sum_j w_qj [F^(-m(j))(x_q) + r_j] is a fold-matched analogue estimate (neighbour label plus the neighbour-excluded refit's predicted difference between query and neighbour). The absorption term M_q = sum_j w_qj [F^full(x_q) - F^(-m(j))(x_q)] measures how much the deployed refit has already moved toward the neighbours it was trained on. For a near-duplicate neighbour and an interpolating expert (trees, TabPFN in-context prediction), M_q is close to r_j, so the naive correction applies the neighbour's error twice. That failure sits where support is densest, which a distance-based novelty schedule cannot damp because it damps the opposite end. Pivot (the runnable fix). Predict yhat_q = (1 - lambda(s_q)) F^full(x_q) + lambda(s_q) A_q. In A_q the base model, the transfer and the borrowed residual all come from a refit that saw neither q nor j, so M_q is removed rather than damped. Here s_q = (delta_1, n_eff, sigma_A) is a support descriptor: delta_1 is rho to the nearest training composition, n_eff = (sum of unnormalised kernel masses)^2 / (sum of squared masses), and sigma_A is the w-weighted dispersion of the per-neighbour transfer terms. The damping lambda maps s to [0, lambda_max] with lambda_max at most 1, drawn from a low-capacity admissible family Lambda (logistic in s with sign constraints, or isotonic in n_eff) that contains lambda = 0. Manufactured signal (the companion). The deployment-optimal damping lambda*(s) cannot be estimated from out-of-fold residuals alone, because those do not stand in the deployed fold relation. So for every i in P_m the stack builds a deployment-matched instance: the 'deployed' prediction is F^(-m)(x_i); the analogue A_i = sum over j outside P_m of w_ij [F^(-m,-m(j))(x_i) + y_j - F^(-m,-m(j))(x_j)] uses refits that excluded both i's and j's folds; s_i is computed against T_k minus P_m. Then i relates to F^(-m) exactly as an outer test composition relates to F^full, up to the training set being one inner fold smaller. Lambda, h, k_nn, rho and tau are fit or selected by minimising the realised loss of (1 - lambda(s_i)) F^(-m)(x_i) + lambda(s_i) A_i on these instances, with selection cross-validated grouped by m. Because lambda = 0 is admissible, the selected correction's realised in-fold effect is non-negative relative to the uncorrected stack by construction (empirical grade; its transfer to outer test is the falsification target), and it switches off wherever thin evidence makes A noisy, with no new labels acquired.
phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.core_mechanism_reasoning: BLOCK 1 — PREMISES. (P1) The out-of-fold errors of global composition stacks on these tasks co-vary within chemical neighbourhoods. Reason: Matbench composition data are chemically clustered and redundant (arxiv:2005.00707), and correction need tracks local coverage (semanticscholar:398586587c1f70079b3b60825e93ff651a519ff9). Untested on these tasks — falsification target, because if it is false A_q carries no signal and lambda collapses to 0. (P2) Interpolating experts absorb their training neighbours, so M_q is large exactly when delta_1 is small. Reason: tree ensembles and in-context TabPFN predict near-duplicates of training points close to those points' labels. Untested — falsification target and the load-bearing bet of the hook. (P3, OBSERVATION MODEL) Outer test compositions are drawn from T_k's dataset by the official random 5-fold split, so a test composition's neighbourhood in T_k, and its fold relation to F^full, are distributed like a manufactured instance's neighbourhood in T_k minus P_m and its fold relation to F^(-m). The residual biases are (a) a one-fold-smaller training set, which slightly lowers near-duplicate density and raises base error in manufactured instances, and (b) correlated instances, because a composition appears as a neighbour in many instances. (a) is the same small-sample shift every nested CV tolerates; (b) is handled by grouping selection by m. The premise would be false under a cluster or chemical-system split, so the claim is scoped to the official random folds. Untested — falsification target via the near-duplicate stratum. (P4) The residual scale tau keeps the transfer meaningful for classification. Reason: additive transfer on the probability scale can leave [0,1], so the logit working residual is admissible and the choice is made by nested CV. ESTIMAND: the expected per-composition loss (absolute error; log loss for classification) of yhat on compositions drawn as the official outer test fold is drawn from the task dataset, overall and conditional on delta_1 stratum. The damping's target is lambda*(s) = argmin over Lambda of E[loss(y, (1 - lambda) F^full + lambda A) | s] under that same draw; the manufactured instances estimate it under P3. BLOCK 2 — NAIVE-BASELINE AUDIT. Naive version: add the kernel-weighted out-of-fold residuals of the k_nn nearest training compositions to the full-refit stack prediction, scaled by a novelty damping that decays with distance, and tune h, k_nn and the decay by nested CV on out-of-fold residuals. Branch (i): it relies on the false premise that a neighbour's out-of-fold residual is the deployed refit's error at the query (M_q = 0). Under random folds on redundant data with interpolating experts, M_q is largest at the near-duplicate end, so the naive correction double-counts there. And because its tuning signal is itself out-of-fold, where M is identically 0, nested CV cannot see the failure. The mechanism confronts this by removing M_q through fold matching and by fitting the damping on instances that reproduce the deployed fold relation. STANDARD-TOOL FOLLOW-UP: the confrontation borrows cross-fitting (as in double machine learning) and stacking's out-of-fold discipline. The domain-specific structure that the textbook tools do not solve is the coupling of two points' fold memberships, query and borrowed neighbour, in one estimate under compositional redundancy. That coupling forces pair-excluded refits F^(-m,-m'), both for the transfer and for the instances on which the damping is fit; ordinary cross-fitting excludes only the evaluated point. Avoided lineage nodes: the transfer is not regression-kriging or Δ-learning (n_residual_on_input), which borrow in-sample or never-fit residuals; the damping is not partial pooling (C_shrinkage) or an applicability-domain cut-off (C_applicability_domain), since its value is learned from manufactured deployment-matched loss and need not decrease with distance; and no per-query expert weighting is introduced (C_moe, C_des). BLOCK 3 — DESIGN RATIONALE. (a) Anchor-only, because the remaining gaps ask for measurements, which are placed as strata and arms of the falsification rather than as mechanism legs. (b) Alternatives rejected: using in-sample residuals instead (they vanish for interpolating experts, so the correction disappears); averaging the J fold models at test time instead of refitting (this removes M_q for the base prediction but leaves the damping tuned on mismatched instances, and lowers base accuracy at n = 312); a learned per-query gate over experts (lands on C_moe and overfits at this n); a variance-formula shrinkage (cannot represent the near-duplicate failure, because the variance of A is smallest exactly there).
phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.core_mechanism_steps: 1. For outer fold k, load T_k from the official Matbench v0.1 split via the matbench package; compute Magpie and MatMiner composition features (matminer) and element-fraction vectors; never touch the outer test fold until step 10. 2. Partition T_k into J random inner folds; for each expert in the candidate set E, train on T_k minus P_m for each m to get out-of-fold predictions, fit non-negative level-1 weights beta on them, and form F^(-m) and the out-of-fold residuals r_j on scale tau; refit all experts on T_k to form F^full. 3. For each unordered inner-fold pair (m, m'), refit each expert on T_k minus (P_m union P_m') and keep beta fixed, giving F^(-m,-m'); store its predictions on P_m and P_m' (the only points it is ever evaluated at); this is the dominant CPU cost and is parallelised over pairs and experts on the 24 cores. 4. Compute pairwise composition distances under each admissible rho (ElMD; Euclidean on standardised Magpie) between all training compositions, and between each outer test composition and T_k. 5. Build deployment-matched instances: for each i in P_m, take its k_nn nearest compositions outside P_m, compute kernel weights with bandwidth h, the analogue A_i from F^(-m,-m(j)) as defined in core_mechanism, the competing prediction F^(-m)(x_i), and the support descriptor s_i; output a table of (A_i, F^(-m)(x_i), s_i, y_i, m) for every training composition. 6. Fit the damping map: for each candidate (rho, h, k_nn, tau, family in Lambda), fit lambda on instances from all but one inner fold m by minimising the realised loss of (1 - lambda(s)) F^(-m) + lambda(s) A, and score on the held-out m; select the configuration with the lowest grouped-CV loss, with the lambda = 0 configuration always in the candidate set; refit the selected lambda on all instances. 7. Select the expert set E by the same grouped inner CV on the stack's out-of-fold loss before steps 3-6 (so the pair-excluded refits are run only for the selected E). Report the selection outcome and its grouped-CV dispersion. 8. Deployment for outer test composition q: compute A_q from the stored F^(-m(j)) predictions at x_q (each inner fold model predicts q once) and the r_j of its k_nn nearest training compositions, compute s_q against T_k, and output yhat_q = (1 - lambda(s_q)) F^full(x_q) + lambda(s_q) A_q. This changes the submitted prediction, and hence the fold MAE or AUROC, only where the fitted lambda is non-zero. 9. For classification, map yhat_q back to a probability (inverse link when tau is the logit scale, clipping when it is the probability scale), and choose the hard-label threshold inside T_k by the same grouped CV for the balanced-accuracy report. 10. Score yhat on the outer test fold once; record per-composition delta_1 and M_q (the absorption term, computable from the stored predictions) for the stratified analysis; repeat for all five official folds and four tasks.
phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.falsification_prediction: (a) Procedure: on the four Matbench v0.1 composition tasks with official folds, compare arm A0 (the cross-fitted stack F^full), A1 (the naive novelty-damped local out-of-fold correction, all of its knobs tuned by nested CV on out-of-fold residuals), and A2 (the proposed fold-matched correction with manufactured damping). Two ablations: A2a (fold-matched transfer with A1's distance damping) and A2b (naive transfer, which adds M_q back, with damping fit on manufactured instances). Score once per outer fold, and stratify outer-test errors by quantile bins of delta_1 (number of bins a reporting choice, fixed before scoring). (b) If the candidate works: A1's error excess over A0 is concentrated in the smallest-delta_1 stratum and is larger when E contains interpolating experts. A2's MAE (and log loss on expt_is_metal and glass, where both probability AUROC and in-fold-thresholded balanced accuracy are reported separately) is no worse than A0 in every delta_1 stratum, with any gain concentrated in intermediate-support strata; A2 is no worse than A1 overall. (c) Load-bearing variable: the absorption term M_q. Negative control: A2b reinjects M_q while keeping everything else of A2. The prediction is that outer-test MAE in the smallest-delta_1 stratum moves from A2's level back toward A1's, and that the fitted lambda shrinks there, losing A2's intermediate-support gain. A label-permutation control (permute y within each inner fold before building the manufactured instances) should drive the selected lambda to 0 and return the downstream MAE to A0's. Positive control: restrict E to a non-interpolating expert (ridge on Magpie features), where M_q is small by construction; there A1 and A2 should give nearly equal downstream MAE, which isolates M_q as the cause of the A1-A2 difference. All differences are reported per task with fold-level dispersion and a variance-corrected resampled test (Nadeau-Bengio); no numeric gain bar is asserted.
phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.compute_budget: 0 GPU-day, since CPU-only is a hard user constraint, and $0 API. CPU cost on the 24-core workstation is dominated by the pair-excluded refits (J(J-1)/2 per selected expert per outer fold), especially CPU TabPFN v2 on glass and expt_is_metal. A rough estimate is on the order of a few CPU-days for the full four-task campaign including iteration, and much less if TabPFN is excluded by the nested expert selection. differentiation_from_lit.delta: Their GPR Δ-model corrects a universal potential that was never fit to the correction's reference points, and it acquires new DFT labels where support is thin. We construct a correction for a base stack fit on the very compositions whose residuals are borrowed: it removes the resulting absorption term by pair-excluded refits, and it learns where to switch off from manufactured deployment-matched instances, with no label acquisition.

MatterVial fuses latent and symbolic features into one global MODNet and never models the residual it leaves. We add a post-hoc correction stage acting on the out-of-fold residuals of a stack (which may include a MODNet expert), and predict and test where along the nearest-neighbour-distance axis such a stage helps or harms on the same official folds.

ECSG stacks composition experts with one global level-1 rule and no residual stage (abstract-only inference). We keep a global non-negative stack as substrate and construct a fold-matched local residual correction on top of it for the small experimental Matbench tasks.

ICL-FM runs one TabPFN predictor per task on GPU. We use TabPFN on CPU only as one admissible expert, and identify its in-context interpolation of near-duplicate training compositions as a source of the absorption term that makes a naive out-of-fold residual correction double-count.

CORE-STACK+ learns a per-sample gate over experts with large vision pools. We leave expert weights global and learn only a low-capacity per-query damping of a residual transfer, fit on manufactured instances so that it is estimable at n of a few hundred under nested selection.

Matbench fixes random 5-fold splits and nested-CV reference pipelines. We show that, under exactly those random folds, the fold relation between a deployed refit and borrowed out-of-fold residuals is what a local correction must match, and we stratify the evaluation by test-to-train distance, which the protocol leaves uncontrolled.

DSBM assigns each instance a hard best classifier through a meta-model (abstract-only inference). We make no per-instance expert choice and instead blend a fold-matched analogue estimate with one stack prediction by a damping that is zero wherever its manufactured in-fold gain is not positive.

phase2_generate/phase2_generate_output.j.what_step_was_missed: Their Δ-model corrects a base model (CHGNet) trained on different data from the reference points whose residuals the GP borrows, so the borrowed residuals are exchangeable with the query's residual by construction, and thin support is handled by acquiring labels. For the correction to work when the base predictor is trained on the very points whose residuals it borrows, and no labels can be acquired, two further constructions are needed, and they built neither: pair-excluded refits that remove the absorption term from the transfer, and deployment-matched instances on which to learn where the correction must switch off.
